scope: Site performance follow-up after beta Kanban save improvements; reviewed against a snapshot of the existing uncommitted work.
changes: Negative ownership filters use an anti join; mixed Unassigned/caller selections preserve OR semantics without a correlated ownership subplan.
My Work receives the display context in its assignment query and no longer downloads duplicate full record/call details.
Classic employee details request only record data and verification history.
Batch members, totals, metrics and filter options share one calculation and snapshot; catalog count and page share one statement.
Batch pages poll a compact change token, preserve drafts, and refresh only on changes. Provider reconciliation runs after the sync response and cannot block the version read.
AI history starts independently of Overview, downloads individual transcripts on expansion, and defers mounting saved summaries.

Assignment previews return 50 items per requested page, debounce selection changes, and retain a bounded short-lived cache. Allocation facts use one statement instead of five; submit still recalculates the full locked plan.

measurementMethod.description: Bounded READ ONLY PostgreSQL transactions against the configured application database. Measurements are reader/SQL wall times over a pinned connection, not browser latency. Sequential samples have different cache warmth and were collected at different times.

classicDetails.excludes: authentication and optional admin employee-perspective lookup

allocationPlan.excludes: transaction control, endpoint selection resolution, workloads and mutation statements

resolvedFindings.risk: A mixed Unassigned/named-caller OR can retain the slow correlated plan.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Build selectable ID sets with UNION; added call/record parity tests across assignment states.

resolvedFindings.risk: A global source-table fingerprint can make the new polling query expensive.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Restrict source-property and contact versions to batch members; measure the final catalog/detail/legacy queries separately.

resolvedFindings.risk: Reading a version after page data can acknowledge a change that the page did not display.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Read the version before the authoritative page readers.

resolvedFindings.risk: A hung reconciliation request can block committed status reads; a successful read can hide a sync error.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Run sync and version requests independently, bound requests, and maintain separate error state.

resolvedFindings.risk: A rejected allocation followed by cache reuse can keep presenting an obsolete preview.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Clear the preview cache after failures and retries; browser test changes ownership externally and verifies rejection plus recovery.

resolvedFindings.risk: Making preview pagination mandatory breaks existing clients.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Pagination is opt-in via page; requests without it retain the full item list.

resolvedFindings.risk: A deleted call could acquire an incorrect AI-call count during lean hydration.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Keep the legacy zero-count fallback; include a missing-call assignment in field-for-field parity tests.

resolvedFindings.risk: Lazy transcripts could return another execution or employee history.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Reuse authorized history scope, exact deduplicated execution/provider IDs and phone-matched evidence fallback; test unauthorized, dropped, malformed and employee-perspective requests.

additionalChecks: Allocation lock, preview hash, idempotency, ownership, warehouse and exclusion guards remain active.
Paged previews summarize and allocate the entire selection, including rows not on the displayed page.
No-result and out-of-range batch pages preserve whole-batch metrics, filter options and export parity.
Row-version tokens detect older-row edits and deletions; due-time transitions participate in manual detail invalidation.
Aborted requests cannot replace newer history or preview results; caches remain bounded to the current dialog.
Classic employee display fields retain legacy area/rent/city formatting, blocked-call visibility and execution-count behavior.
API compatibility, employee/admin perspectives, responsive layouts and draft preservation were exercised in production-mode Chromium.

validation.database: Disposable PostgreSQL 17, migrations through 023; no application-database mutations.

regularIntegrationTests.note: The eight retained-schema tests passed separately in the shared-schema rehearsal.

sharedSchemaRehearsal.note: Separate temporary local database, upgrade applied twice, original migration ledger preserved; two current-schema-only tests run in the regular suite.

validation.browserNote: Final build: 137 tests followed by 28 tests in disjoint files. The earlier 46-test run is not added again.
validation.buildWarning: The existing Next.js 16.4.3 dependency reports a security advisory. Build completed on retry; no dependency upgrade was included.

remainingLimits: Cold batch-version reads still took up to 3.9 seconds in the final probe, versus 80-194 ms when warm. Initial batch rendering includes this additional token read; end-to-end production latency was not measured.
Manual tokens deliberately include shared assignment/warehouse changes, which can cause a conservative refresh for unrelated work. This avoids silently missing cross-contact ownership changes.
Batch summaries still evaluate the whole batch; very large batches can remain expensive even though repeated calculations and round trips were removed.
Reopen and unassign retain a page refresh to recompute filtered membership, counts and pagination. The legacy ManualAttemptButton currently has no active page consumer.
Lazy transcript history excludes transcript bodies, but the Overview reader retains its existing saved-evidence payload for compatibility.
Provider reconciliation was tested with stubs; no live provider mutation or deployment was performed.
